summary: MSc Data Science student at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg (Apr 2026 - Aug 2028) with applied computer vision and deep learning experience: object detection, face recognition and Convolutional Neural Network training in PyTorch. Co-author of a peer-reviewed paper on deep-learning video surveillance published in the ICISD 2025 proceedings by Atlantis Press (Springer Nature), reporting 95.79% mAP@0.5 for weapon detection. Four applied AI and machine learning roles before the degree, the most recent recognised as Best Performer with 10+ production-ready models delivered. Comfortable owning data preparation, model training and model evaluation end to end. Based in Erlangen.

bullets: Recognised as Best Performer of the cohort: completed 8 end-to-end machine learning projects and delivered 10+ production-ready models across the supervised and unsupervised spectrum.

Prepared data, trained models and reported the evaluation metric that fitted each problem: 95%+ ROC-AUC on a Support Vector Machine tuned by GridSearchCV hyperparameter search, 96%+ accuracy on breast-cancer diagnosis with Logistic Regression, R² above 0.90 on housing-price regression.
Built a Walmart weekly-sales forecasting model with XGBoost, reaching 96.1% R² and reducing forecast error by 18%.
Segmented 200 customers into five actionable clusters with K-Means at a silhouette score of 0.55.
Built an ATS Resume Checker powered by large language models: parsing resumes, scoring them against job descriptions and returning structured feedback.
Designed and iterated LLM prompts and embedding-based retrieval on Google Vertex AI, then set up evaluation loops to measure and improve output quality.
Operated and supported VMware virtualisation infrastructure, automated recurring infrastructure tasks and set up monitoring for cloud workloads.
Built an American Sign Language image-recognition system with a Convolutional Neural Network in PyTorch.
Implemented the full training, validation and inference pipeline, including data augmentation to improve generalisation.

projects.name: PrisonSecure - deep-learning video surveillance
projects.tech: Python, PyTorch, YOLOv11, ResNet, FaceNet, SVM
projects.description: Final-year thesis project: a deep-learning surveillance system for prison environments running on live CCTV feeds. Weapon detection with YOLOv11 and hard negative mining to suppress false positives from visually similar objects; face recognition via a ResNet-based detector, FaceNet embeddings and an SVM classifier; real-time audio alerting on detection. Reported results: 95.79% mAP@0.5 with precision and recall both at 0.93 for weapon detection, and 93.75% accuracy for face recognition.
